source_metadata.title: Pregnancy and Neonatal Outcomes After Fetal Exposure to Biologics and Thiopurines Among Women With Inflammatory Bowel Disease

consistency_findings: Main text reports 133 infants with congenital malformations, while supplemental Table S3 reports 126/1394 with any congenital malformation; the outputs retain table-specific values and do not force reconciliation.
Main Table 4 labels the serum subset n=235, whereas Supplemental Table S2A/Table S11 describe n=234 with concentration data. The difference is retained as source-reported rather than harmonized.

Several isolated ASQ3 domain comparisons have nominal P<0.05, but the source conclusion is based on the lack of a consistent adverse developmental pattern; no multiplicity correction is reported in the supplied article.
extraction_limitations: The atom model has no dedicated field for study-level metadata, cohort flow diagrams, or multiplicity-adjusted interpretation; these are carried in coverage/validation metadata and tags.

The current quantitative_result schema requires one numeric estimate per atom, so multi-arm tables are represented as selected independently reviewable contrasts rather than as a complete cell-for-cell table dump.
The supplement contains extensive descriptive tables; key results and interpretation-relevant analyses were atomized, but routine descriptive cells were not converted into individual atoms.
schema_gaps: No dedicated atom kind for sample-size/power statements or cohort-flow accounting; represented as method/population/limitation atoms.
No structured field for global/multiplicity-adjusted p-values across multiple arms; these are kept in original_result_text or qualitative atoms when a single effect estimate is not defensible.
